bottom_line: In patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by left ventricular dysfunction and heart failure, eplerenone vs placebo reduced death from any cause (relative risk, 0.85; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.75 to 0.96).
implications: These data support that, over a mean follow-up of 16 months, adding eplerenone to optimal medical therapy (vs placebo) reduced all-cause mortality (478 vs 554 deaths; relative risk, 0.85; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.75 to 0.96) and reduced the composite of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for cardiovascular events (26.7 percent vs 30.0 percent; relative risk, 0.87), while increasing serious hyperkalemia (5.5 percent vs 3.9 percent).

major_points.text: Multicenter, international, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial design.
major_points.quote: We conducted a multicenter, international, random- ized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.

major_points.text: Patients were assigned to eplerenone (starting 25 mg daily, titrated up to 50 mg daily) or matching placebo, in addition to optimal medical therapy.
major_points.quote: Patients were randomly assigned to eplerenone (25 mg per day initially, titrated to a maximum of 50 mg per day; 3313 patients) or placebo (3319 patients) in addition to op- timal medical therapy.

major_points.text: The two primary end points included death from any cause and a composite of cardiovascular death or cardiovascular hospitalization.
major_points.quote: The two primary end points were time to death from any cause and time to death from cardiovascular causes or first hospitalization for a cardiovascular event, including heart failure, recurrent acute myo- cardial infarction, stroke, or ventricular arrhythmia.

major_points.text: Eplerenone reduced death from any cause compared with placebo.
major_points.quote: there were 478 deaths in the eplerenone group and 554 deaths in the placebo group (relative risk, 0.85; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.75 to 0.96; P=0.008).

major_points.text: Eplerenone reduced the composite primary end point of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for cardiovascular events compared with placebo.
major_points.quote: The end point of death from cardiovascular causes or hospitalization for cardiovascular events was reached by 885 patients in the eplerenone group (26.7 percent) and 993 patients in the placebo group (30.0 percent) (relative risk, 0.87; P=0.002)

major_points.text: Serious hyperkalemia occurred more often with eplerenone, while hypokalemia occurred less often with eplerenone.
major_points.quote: Serious hyperkalemia (serum po- tassium concentration, ≥6.0 mmol per liter) oc- curred in 5.5 percent of patients in the eplerenone group, as compared with 3.9 percent of those in the placebo group (P=0.002).

absolute_effects.text: Deaths: 478 in the eplerenone group vs 554 in the placebo group.
absolute_effects.quote: there were 478 deaths in the eplerenone group and 554 deaths in the placebo group

absolute_effects.text: Composite primary end point (cardiovascular death or hospitalization for cardiovascular events): 26.7 percent vs 30.0 percent.
absolute_effects.quote: reached by 885 patients in the eplerenone group (26.7 percent) and 993 patients in the placebo group (30.0 percent)

absolute_effects.text: Kaplan–Meier estimates of one-year mortality: 11.8 percent vs 13.6 percent.
absolute_effects.quote: Kaplan–Meier estimates of mortality at one year were 11.8 percent in the eplerenone group and 13.6 percent in the placebo group

absolute_effects.text: Estimated number needed to treat: 50 to save one life in one year; 33 to prevent one cardiovascular death or one cardiovascular hospitalization in one year.
absolute_effects.quote: with an estimated number need- ed to treat of 50 to save one life in one year and an estimated number needed to treat of 33 to prevent one death from cardiovascular causes or one hospi- talization for a cardiovascular event in one year

subgroups.text: Subgroup analyses for the two primary end points were performed with a Cox model stratified according to region with treatment, subgroup, and interaction terms.
subgroups.quote: Subgroup analyses for the two primary end points were performed with a Cox model stratified accord- ing to region, with terms for treatment, subgroup, and interaction between treatment and subgroup.

subgroups.text: The beneficial effect of eplerenone was consistent across geographic regions (interaction P values reported for both primary end points).
subgroups.quote: The beneficial effect of eplerenone was also consistent across geographic regions (P= 0.24 for the interaction of treatment and region for death from any cause, and P=0.94 for the interaction of treatment and region for death

subgroups.text: Authors state the trial was not powered for definitive conclusions in individual subgroups.
subgroups.quote: our trial was not designed with sufficient power to draw statistical conclusions about individual sub- groups.

harms.text: Serious hyperkalemia (serum potassium ≥6.0 mmol per liter) occurred more often with eplerenone.
harms.quote: Serious hyperkalemia (serum po- tassium concentration, ≥6.0 mmol per liter) oc- curred in 5.5 percent of patients in the eplerenone group, as compared with 3.9 percent of those in the placebo group (P=0.002).

harms.text: Serious hypokalemia (serum potassium <3.5 mmol/liter) occurred less often with eplerenone.
Permanent discontinuation of study medication occurred in both groups.

inclusion_criteria.text: Eligible for randomization 3 to 14 days after acute myocardial infarction.
inclusion_criteria.quote: were eligible for randomization 3 to 14 days after acute myocardial infarction:

inclusion_criteria.text: Left ventricular dysfunction documented by a left ventricular ejection fraction of 40 percent or lower before randomization.
inclusion_criteria.quote: left ventricular dysfunction as documented by a left ventricular ejection fraction of 40 percent or lower on echocardiography, radionuclide angiog- raphy, or angiography of the left ventricle after the index acute myocardial infarction and before ran- domization;

inclusion_criteria.text: Heart failure documented by pulmonary rales, pulmonary venous congestion on chest radiography, or a third heart sound.
inclusion_criteria.quote: heart failure as documented by the presence of pulmonary rales, chest radiography showing pulmonary venous congestion, or the pres- ence of a third heart sound.

inclusion_criteria.text: In patients with diabetes who met criteria for left ventricular dysfunction after acute myocardial infarction, symptoms of heart failure did not have to be demonstrated.
inclusion_criteria.quote: In patients with diabe- tes who met the criteria for left ventricular dysfunc- tion after acute myocardial infarction, symptoms of heart failure did not have to be demonstrated

exclusion_criteria.quote: Important criteria for exclusion were the use of potassium-sparing diuretics

exclusion_criteria.text: Serum creatinine concentration of more than 2.5 mg per deciliter (220 µmol per liter).
exclusion_criteria.quote: a serum creatinine concentration of more than 2.5 mg per deciliter (220 µmol per liter)

exclusion_criteria.text: Serum potassium concentration of more than 5.0 mmol per liter before randomization.

analysis_methods.text: Primary and secondary end points compared using Cox proportional-hazards regression stratified by geographic region.
analysis_methods.quote: with the use of Cox proportional-hazards regres- sion. The Cox model included a single covariate cor- responding to treatment group and was stratified according to geographic region

analysis_methods.text: Analyses of the primary and secondary end points were conducted according to the intention-to-treat principle.
analysis_methods.quote: Analyses of the primary and secondary end points were conducted according to the inten- tion-to-treat principle.

analysis_methods.text: The trial was designed to enroll 6200 patients and continue until 1012 deaths occurred.
analysis_methods.quote: The trial was designed to enroll 6200 patients and to continue until 1012 deaths occurred.

analysis_methods.text: With testing at the 0.04 level, the study had 88.3 percent power to detect an 18.5 percent difference in the rate of death from any cause.

analysis_methods.text: Reported P values were two-sided and not adjusted for interim analyses.
